buyer: Sponsors and, indirectly, her own client pipeline
pain: n/a - this is a distribution asset rather than a product
v1: Ten episodes with guests from both worlds
channel: Her two networks as guests, public as audience
verdict: A poor business and possibly an excellent marketing channel - worth doing for the wrong reason.

why.distribution: Guest access is outstanding; audience access is nonexistent.
why.demand: Nobody pays for podcasts, and sponsors only appear at scale she will not reach quickly.
why.fmf: She can convene both worlds credibly and ask genuinely good questions.
why.defensibility: The guest access and the two-world positioning are genuinely hard to copy.
why.tailwind: Podcast advertising is soft and the market is saturated.
why.ceiling: £2k x 30 sponsored episodes = £60k, and reaching sponsorship scale takes years.

ceiling_arithmetic: £2k x 30 sponsored episodes = £60k, but sponsorship requires audience scale that takes years. Year one revenue is realistically zero. Structurally capped as a business.
carries: Outstanding guest access, and every episode is a warm conversation with a potential client.
kills: It is not a business. Judged as revenue it fails on every axis.
test: Record five episodes and count how many guests become client conversations.
test_pass: Two guests ask about working with her - which means it is marketing, and should be judged as such.
